'''Fiat India Automobiles Private Ltd''' ('''FIAPL''') is an Indian [[automobile manufacturing]] company located in [[Ranjangaon]] near [[Pune]], Maharastra, jointly owned by [[Stellantis]] and [[Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles|Tata Motors]].

== History ==
[[Fiat S.p.A.|Fiat]] and Tata first formed the partnership in February 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/business/2026/Feb/10/tata-motors-pv-and-stellantis-ink-mou-to-explore-future-collaboration-opportunities|title=Tata Motors PV and Stellantis ink MoU to explore future collaboration opportunities|date=10 February 2026|access-date=2 July 2026|last=Khan|first=Arshad|work=The New Indian Express}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/stellantis-turns-to-tata-motors-to-build-global-jeep-out-of-india/article71007701.ece|title=Stellantis turns to Tata Motors to build global Jeep out of India|date=21 May 2026|access-date=2 July 2026|last=Mohile|first=Amit Vijay|work=The Hindu Business Line}}</ref> The agreement was meant to give Tata access to Fiat's multi-jet diesel engines.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/t-companies/tata-motors/tata-motors-fiat-chart-a-winning-formula/articleshow/1815182.cms|title=Tata Motors, Fiat chart a winning formula|date=27 July 2006|access-date=4 July 2026|work=[[The Economic Times]]}}</ref> Fiat already had [[Stellantis India|its Indian operations]] located at the Ranjangaon plant.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/fiat-spells-details-tata-motors-alliance-2083|title=Fiat spells out details of Tata Motors alliance|date=15 February 2007|access-date=5 July 2026|work=Autocar Professional}}</ref> The plant was expected to produce passenger cars, engines and transmissions for both Indian market and export. Tata said US$650 million would be invested into the plant. In October 2007, production was reported to exceed 100,000 cars and 200,000 engines and transmissions, and provide direct and indirect employment to over 4,000 people. That month, [[Fiat Palio]] production commenced.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.domain-b.com/companies-organisations/firms-companies/tata-motors-signs-car-engine-joint-venture-with-fiat|title=Tata Motors signs car, engine joint venture with Fiat|date=11 October 2007|access-date=4 July 2026|work=Domain B}}</ref>

The joint venture has produced [[Fiat JTD engine#1.2 JTDm/Multijet/CDTI/D/DDiS/HDi|1.3 Multijet engine]] and corresponding powertrains common to a number for supply to the [[Fiat Palio]], [[Fiat Grande Punto]], [[Fiat Linea]], [[Fiat Avventura]], Fiat Urban Cross, [[Tata Vista]] [[Tata Manza]], as well as [[Premier Automobiles Limited|Premier]]'s Rio and [[Maruti Suzuki]]'s [[Suzuki S-Cross|S-Cross]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/news/passenger-vehicle/uv/maruti-to-source-1-6-litre-diesel-fiat-engine-for-s-cross-developing-own-1-5-litre-engine/articleshow/47611088.cms | title=Maruti to source 1.6 litre diesel Fiat engine for S-Cross; developing own 1.5 litre engine | date=10 June 2015 | newspaper=The Economic Times | access-date=30 December 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/vQNIluEPZECxpsLAj2Oz2J/Fiat-to-power-Premier8217s-Rio.html | title=Fiat to power Premier's Rio | date=17 May 2012 | publisher=Live Mint | first=Shally Seth | last=Mohile | access-date=30 December 2018 }}</ref>

Fiat merged with American automaker [[Chrysler]] on 12 October 2014, with the resulting entity named [[Fiat Chrysler Automobiles]] (FCA).<ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.detroitnews.com/story/business/autos/chrysler/2014/10/07/fiat-chrysler-automobiles-merger-cleared/16851393/ |title=Fiat Chrysler Automobiles merger to become official Sunday |date=7 October 2014 |first=Michael |last=Wayland |newspaper=The Detroit News |access-date=26 February 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.reuters.com/article/us-fiat-spa-chrysler-idUSKCN0HW0CZ20141007 |title=Fiat says merger into Dutch-registered FCA effective October 12 |work=Reuters |date=7 October 2014 |access-date=26 February 2015}}</ref> In February 2016, FCA announced it would launch the [[Jeep]] brand, inherited from Chrysler, in India, with a new model to begin production at the Ranjangaon plant in 2017;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/jeep-debuts-india-wrangler-grand-cherokee-10350|title=Jeep debuts in India with Wrangler and Grand Cherokee|date=3 February 2016|access-date=8 July 2026|work=Autocar Professional}}</ref> it had previously announced plans to invest US$280 million into the plant to support production of a Jeep model in July 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/fiat-chrysler-automobiles-invest-rs-768-ranjangaon-plant-jeep-model-8760|title=Fiat Chrysler Automobiles to invest Rs 1,768 crore in new Ranjangaon plant for Jeep model|date=1 July 2015|access-date=8 July 2026|work=Autocar Professional}}</ref> On 1 June 2017, the first locally produced [[Jeep Compass]] rolled off the assembly line.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/-india-jeep-compass-rolls-assembly-line-ranjangaon-24848|title=First made-in-India Jeep Compass rolls out|date=1 June 2017|access-date=8 July 2026|work=Autocar Professional}}</ref> Exports to other [[right-hand drive]] markets commenced in October.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/india-jeep-compass-sets-sail-hand-drive-markets-26736|title=India-made Jeep Compass sets sail for right-hand-drive markets|date=25 October 2017|access-date=8 July 2026|work=Autocar Professional}}</ref>

In May 2017, FCA signed a contract for the production and supply of the [[Fiat JTD engine#2.0 JTDm/CDTI/TiD/TTiD/VCDi/Multijet II/DDiS|2.0 liter ''Multijet II'' turbo diesel engines]] to Tata.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://carandbike.com/news/fiat-india-renews-agreement-to-supply-diesel-engines-to-tata-motors-and-maruti-suzuki-1689103|title=Fiat India To Also Supply Bigger Diesel Engines To Tata Motors And Maruti Suzuki|publisher=carandbike.com |date=3 May 2017|access-date=15 January 2019}}</ref> The 2.0-liter ''Multijet II'' engine in the same year went into production at the Indian Ranjangaon plant to be adopted by the Jeep Compass also produced locally. The supply to Tata Motors concerns about 70,000 per year to be fitted to the [[Tata Harrier]] SUV that went into production at the end of 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/upcoming-tata-harrier-suv-to-get-20l-kryotec-diesel-engine-40932 |title=Upcoming Tata Harrier SUV to get 2.0L Kryotec diesel engine |publisher=autocarpro.in |date=7 October 2018|accessdate=2 January 2019}}</ref> It has also been used by [[JSW MG Motor India|MG]] in the [[MG Hector|Hector]] since 2019,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-06-28|title=MG Hector Receives 10,000 Bookings In 23 Days|url=https://carandbike.com/news/mg-hector-receives-10-000-bookings-in-23-days-2060063|access-date=2019-07-06|website=NDTV CarAndBike|language=en-EN}}</ref> and in the [[Tata Safari]] since 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gravitas to be launched as the new Tata Safari|url=https://www.autocarindia.com/car-news/gravitas-to-be-launched-as-the-new-tata-safari-419572|access-date=2021-01-06|website=Autocar India|language=en}}</ref>

In November 2018, FCA discontinued the [[Fiat]] brand in India due to low sales, with production of the Fiat Punto models (including the [[Abarth]] version), Avventura and Linea ending.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rushlane.com/fiat-punto-linea-to-be-discontinued-12288421.html|title=Fiat Punto, Linea to be discontinued from India – Production stopped| publisher=rushlane.com |date=21 November 2018 |access-date= 14 January 2014}}</ref>

In September 2023, the plant's paint shop briefly caught fire. A Tata Motors spokesperson said the incident was brought under control "very quickly" and that it would not impact supply.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autocarpro.in/news/fire-broke-out-at-fiat-indias-ranjangaon-plant-this-week-jv-partner-tata-motors-assures-production-not-hampered-116910|title=Fire broke out at Fiat India's Ranjangaon plant this week, JV partner Tata Motors assures production not hampered|date=23 September 2023|access-date=8 July 2026|work=Autocar Professional}}</ref>

== Production ==
=== Current models ===
* [[Jeep Compass]] (2017–present)
* [[Tata Nexon]] (2017–present)
* [[Tata Altroz]] (2020–present)
* [[Jeep Wrangler (JL)|Jeep Wrangler]] (2021–present, [[Knock-down kit|CKD assembly]])
* [[Jeep Commander (2022)|Jeep Meridian/Commander]] (2022–present)
* [[Jeep Grand Cherokee]] (2022–present, [[Knock-down kit|CKD assembly]])
* [[Tata Curvv]] (2024–present)

=== Former models ===
* [[Fiat Palio]] (2007–2010)
* [[Fiat Grande Punto]] (2008–2014)
* [[Fiat Linea]] (2008–2018)
* [[Tata Zest]] (2014–2019)
* [[Fiat Punto Evo]] (2014–2018)
* [[Fiat Avventura]] (2014–2018)
